For acute deep vein thrombosis (DVT) or pulmonary embolism (PE) without cancer, **direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs)** are recommended as first-line therapy over vitamin K antagonists like warfarin [ACCP, 2021]. The ACCP guideline specifies that anticoagulation should last at least 3 months, with indefinite extension for unprovoked events in low bleeding risk patients [ACCP, 2021](https://journal.chestnet.org/article/S0012-3692(21)01506-3/fulltext).

**Note:** Specific DOACs (e.g., rivaroxaban, apixaban, dabigatran) are commonly used but were not explicitly mentioned in the retrieved guideline excerpt. Clinical decisions should consider individual patient factors and local guidelines. 

*Citation: Antithrombotic Therapy for VTE Disease, ACCP, 2021*
